## Purpose of this document and where it goes in the paper

**Question.** For a measles introduction into a school, how much does each
tiered quarantine strategy (days of quarantine for high / medium / low-risk
contacts) change the size of the outbreak, and **why**?

**Why fair pairs.** With an ordinary simulation, two strategies run on the same
seed share the same outbreak only until the first case is detected; after that
each student's disease course and contacts are re-drawn, so part of the
difference between strategies is chance. Here every strategy is run on the
**same 2000 outbreaks** with the **same dice for every student**, so every
difference in this document is caused only by the quarantine rules (and, across
tables, by vaccination coverage and the school's contact pattern).

**What this document provides, and where each part fits in a paper:**

| Part of this document | What it shows | Where in the paper |
|---|---|---|
| Model assumptions and criteria | states, parameters, quarantine rules, definitions | **Methods** (model description) + a supplementary table |
| Model behaviour in the simulations | how long students stay latent / contagious / at home | **Methods** or **Supplement** (shows the rules in action, e.g. that a 0-day quarantine = 1 day at home) |
| Is the comparison fair? | 100% of students have the same disease course under every strategy | **Methods** (one sentence + the number) |
| Tables A and B (by school) | outbreak probabilities, paired differences with 95% CI, run-by-run comparison, cost in healthy days at home | **Results** (main tables) |
| Summary across schools | average change in cases vs 21/21/21, how often 21/21/21 did better / same / worse | **Results** (main figure + table) |
| Where do infections come from? (Table 1) | infections before detection, from students never sent home, from students sent home only briefly, from students back from a real quarantine | **Results** (mechanism) and **Discussion** |
| What happened to each infected student? (Table 2) | how often quarantine contained an infected student, and how many others the rest infected | **Results / Discussion** |
| Why do strategies differ? | change vs 21/21/21 split by where the infections came from | **Discussion** (explains the result) |
| Grade-to-grade spread and example outbreaks | how infections move between grades; one fair example per school | **Supplement** (illustrations) |

::: {.callout-note}
Needs the modified ("common random numbers") measles package installed in its
own library (default `~/R_libs_crn`, change with the `MEASLES_LIB` environment
variable). Simulations are cached in `results/crn_*.csv`; delete them to
re-run. Quick test: `N_PAIRS=200 N_DETAIL=200 quarto render 07_fair_pairs_tables.qmd`.
:::

## Model assumptions and criteria

This section lists everything the model assumes, so the results can be read
against it. Values are read from the model itself.

### Disease states

| State | Meaning | Contagious? | At school? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Susceptible | not infected (unvaccinated, or vaccinated with vaccine failure possible) | no | yes |
| Latent | infected, not yet contagious | no | yes |
| Prodromal | contagious, no rash yet | **yes (the only contagious state)** | yes |
| Rash | rash has appeared, not yet noticed | no | yes |
| Isolated / Isolated recovered | rash noticed: kept home for the isolation period | no | no |
| Hospitalized | in hospital | no | no |
| Recovered | immune | no | yes |
| Quarantined susceptible / latent / prodromal | sent home as a contact; same disease progression as at school | latent/prodromal continue at home, but cannot infect anyone at school | no |

### Parameters

```{r params}
pm <- local({
  s <- SCHOOLS[1]; sizes <- ENROLLMENT[[s]]; n <- sum(sizes)
  m <- ModelMeaslesMixingRiskQuarantine(n = n, prevalence = 1 / n,
    contact_matrix = SCHOOL_CMAT[[s]], transmission_rate = TRANS_RATE[[s]],
    prop_vaccinated = 0.7, detection_rate_quarantine = 0.0, contact_tracing_days_window = 7,
    quarantine_period_high = 21L, quarantine_period_medium = 21L, quarantine_period_low = 21L)
  g <- function(p) tryCatch(get_param(m, p), error = function(e) NA)
  data.table(
    Parameter = c("Incubation period", "Prodromal period", "Rash period", "Days undetected",
                  "Isolation period", "Hospitalization rate", "Hospitalization period",
                  "Vax efficacy", "Contact tracing days window", "Contact tracing success rate",
                  "Detection rate quarantine", "Quarantine willingness", "Isolation willingness"),
    `How the model uses it` = c(
      "mean days latent; each day a latent student becomes contagious with probability 1/value",
      "mean days contagious; each day a contagious student develops the rash with probability 1/value",
      "each day with a rash: recovers with probability 1/value",
      "each day with a rash: the rash is noticed (detection) with probability 1/value",
      "days kept home after the rash appears, once detected",
      "each day with a rash: hospitalized with this probability (competes with recovery)",
      "mean days in hospital",
      "a vaccinated student's chance of infection is reduced by this proportion (per contact)",
      "contacts in this many days before the rash count as traced (medium-risk) contacts",
      "share of contacts that are traced",
      "chance a student who develops a rash while in quarantine is detected",
      "share of students who comply with quarantine",
      "share of students who comply with isolation"),
    Value = vapply(c("Incubation period", "Prodromal period", "Rash period", "Days undetected",
                     "Isolation period", "Hospitalization rate", "Hospitalization period",
                     "Vax efficacy", "Contact tracing days window", "Contact tracing success rate",
                     "Detection rate quarantine", "Quarantine willingness", "Isolation willingness"),
                   function(p) format(g(p)), character(1)))
})
knitr::kable(pm, align = "llr", caption = "Disease and intervention parameters used in every run.")

knitr::kable(rbindlist(lapply(SCHOOLS, function(s) data.table(
  School = s, Grades = length(ENROLLMENT[[s]]), Students = sum(ENROLLMENT[[s]]),
  `Transmission rate (per contact)` = signif(TRANS_RATE[[s]], 3),
```

### Rules for contacts, detection and quarantine

1. **Contacts.** Each day, each student at school has contacts with students of
   every grade at the rate given by the school's contact matrix. The chance of
   meeting a particular contagious student is that rate divided by the number
   of students of that grade **who are at school** (capped at 1). An infected
   contact passes measles with the transmission rate (reduced by the vaccine for
   vaccinated students). Students at home have no contacts.
2. **Only the prodromal stage is contagious.** Once the rash appears the
   student is no longer contagious.
3. **Detection.** Each day a student has a rash, it is noticed with probability
   1/*days undetected*. The day it is noticed is a **detection**.
4. **Who is sent home.** At the **end of each detection day**, every
   **unvaccinated** student who is not already at home is sent home, with a
   quarantine length set by their risk tier:
   - **high risk**: every unvaccinated student in the **same grade** as the detected case;
   - **medium risk**: unvaccinated students in other grades who had **contact with the detected case** in the 7 days before its rash;
   - **low risk**: every other unvaccinated student.

   Vaccinated students are **never** quarantined.
5. **How long.** A student is released when *days since being sent home e
   quarantine days for their tier*. The check happens at the next day's update,
   so **N days of quarantine = N days at home, and 0 days = 1 day at home**
   (the day after detection). In other words, "0" is not "no quarantine": every
   unvaccinated student misses one school day per detection.
6. **No extension.** A student who is already at home when another case is
   detected keeps their original release day.
7. **Disease continues at home.** A quarantined student who is infected keeps
   progressing (latent  contagious  rash) at home; they return on their
   release day in whatever state they are in (possibly still latent or already
   contagious). A student whose rash appears at home is isolated.
8. **Stage durations are geometric**: each day the same chance of moving on
   (e.g. 1/12 per day to leave the latent stage), so durations vary widely
   (see the next section and document 6).

### Outcomes and definitions used below

- **Outbreak size** = number of students infected by day `r N_DAYS`, including the first case.
- **First detection** = the first day a rash is noticed (the student is isolated, or goes straight to hospital) and the first students are sent home.
- **Healthy student-days at home** = days spent at home by students who were never infected (the cost of quarantine).
- **A real quarantine** = a continuous stay at home of at least `r MIN_HOME` days in a row. Single days at home (from 0-day quarantines), or a few single days in a row when cases are detected on consecutive days, are counted separately as **brief stays at home**.

```{r detail-functions}
## ---- Model with optional daily state recorder ------------------------------
rec <- new.env()
build_model <- function(school, vacc, duration, record = FALSE) {
  sizes <- ENROLLMENT[[school]]; n <- sum(sizes)
  m <- ModelMeaslesMixingRiskQuarantine(
    n = n, prevalence = 1 / n,
    contact_matrix = SCHOOL_CMAT[[school]], transmission_rate = TRANS_RATE[[school]],
    prop_vaccinated = vacc, detection_rate_quarantine = 0.0,
    contact_tracing_days_window = 7,
    quarantine_period_high   = as.integer(duration[1]),
    quarantine_period_medium = as.integer(duration[2]),
    quarantine_period_low    = as.integer(duration[3]))
  for (k in seq_along(sizes))
    m <- add_entity(m, entity("Grade", as.integer(sizes[k]), FALSE))
  if (record) {
    f  <- function(m) rec$days[[length(rec$days) + 1L]] <- get_agents_states(m)
    ge <- globalevent_fun(f, "State recorder")
    rec$keep[[length(rec$keep) + 1L]] <- list(f, ge, m)   # keep R from garbage-collecting it
    m <- add_globalevent(m, ge)
  }
  verbose_off(m)
  m
}
parse_strat <- function(s) as.integer(strsplit(s, "/")[[1]])
student_grades <- function(m) {
  ents <- get_entities(m); g <- integer(0)
  for (k in seq_along(ents)) { a <- as.data.table(entity_get_agents(ents[[k]])); g[a$agent + 1L] <- k }
  g
}
longest_run <- function(x) if (!length(x) || !any(x)) 0L else { r <- rle(x); max(r$lengths[r$values]) }

## ---- Where each infection came from ----------------------------------------
KINDS <- c("Before anyone was detected",
           "From a student never sent home",
           sprintf("From a student sent home only briefly (1-%d days)", MIN_HOME - 1),
           sprintf("From a student back from a real quarantine (%d+ days)", MIN_HOME))
KIND_COLS <- setNames(c("#B4B2A9", "#D85A30", "#EF9F27", "#1D9E75"), KINDS)
GROUPS2 <- c("Contagious period fully at home",
             sprintf("Back from a real quarantine (%d+ days) still infected", MIN_HOME),
             sprintf("Home only 1-%d days while infected, contagious at school", MIN_HOME - 1),
             "Never sent home while infected",
             "Still latent on the last day")
QSTATES <- c("Quarantined Susceptible", "Quarantined Latent",
             "Quarantined Prodromal", "Quarantined Recovered")
ALL_STATES <- c("Susceptible", "Latent", "Prodromal", "Rash", "Isolated", "Isolated Recovered",
                "Quarantined Susceptible", "Quarantined Latent", "Quarantined Prodromal",
                "Quarantined Recovered", "Hospitalized", "Recovered")

## One run with full detail
detail_run <- function(m, seed) {
  rec$days <- list()
  run(m, ndays = N_DAYS, seed = seed)
  S  <- do.call(rbind, rec$days)
  gr <- student_grades(m)
  tr <- as.data.table(get_transmissions(m))[, .(date, source, target)]
  isQ <- S %in% QSTATES; dim(isQ) <- dim(S)
  ## first detection: first day a rash is noticed. A detected student is isolated,
  ## or goes straight to hospital; either way the quarantine starts that same day.
  det <- which(rowSums(S == "Isolated" | S == "Isolated Recovered" | isQ) > 0)
  first_det <- if (length(det)) min(det) else NA_integer_

  ## infections, classified by the infector's longest stay at home before infecting
  e <- tr[source >= 0]
  e[, `:=`(src_grade = gr[source + 1L], tgt_grade = gr[target + 1L])]
  e[, days_home := mapply(function(s, d) longest_run(isQ[seq_len(max(d - 1L, 0L)), s + 1L]), source, date)]
  e[, kind := fifelse(is.na(first_det) | date <= first_det, KINDS[1],
              fifelse(days_home == 0L, KINDS[2],
              fifelse(days_home < MIN_HOME, KINDS[3], KINDS[4])))]

  ## infected students (first case excluded)
  st <- tr[source >= 0, .(id = target, inf_day = date, grade = gr[target + 1L])]
  col <- function(i) S[, i + 1L]
  st[, `:=`(
    latent_days   = vapply(id, function(i) { d <- which(col(i) %in% c("Prodromal", "Quarantined Prodromal"))
                                             if (length(d)) min(d) - inf_day[match(i, id)] else NA_real_ }, numeric(1)),
    contag_days   = vapply(id, function(i) sum(col(i) %in% c("Prodromal", "Quarantined Prodromal")), integer(1)),
    contag_school = vapply(id, function(i) sum(col(i) == "Prodromal"), integer(1)),
    quar_inf_days = vapply(id, function(i) longest_run(col(i) %in% c("Quarantined Latent", "Quarantined Prodromal")), integer(1)),
    hosp          = vapply(id, function(i) any(col(i) == "Hospitalized"), logical(1)),
    isolated      = vapply(id, function(i) any(col(i) %in% c("Isolated", "Isolated Recovered")), logical(1)))]
  ninf <- e[, .N, by = source]
  st[, n_infected := ninf$N[match(id, ninf$source)]][is.na(n_infected), n_infected := 0L]
  st[, group := fcase(contag_days == 0L,                          GROUPS2[5],
                      quar_inf_days > 0L & contag_school == 0L,   GROUPS2[1],
                      quar_inf_days >= MIN_HOME,                  GROUPS2[2],
                      quar_inf_days > 0L,                         GROUPS2[3],
                      default =                                   GROUPS2[4])]

  ## every stay at home in quarantine (all students), by length
  stays <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(ncol(isQ)), function(i) { r <- rle(isQ[, i]); r$lengths[r$values] }))
  runs <- data.table(run = seed, size = nrow(tr), grades_reached = uniqueN(gr[tr$target + 1L]),
                     first_det = first_det,
                     stays_1 = sum(stays == 1), stays_2_6 = sum(stays %in% 2:6),
                     stays_7_20 = sum(stays %in% 7:20), stays_21p = sum(stays >= 21),
                     healthy_days_home = sum(S == "Quarantined Susceptible"))
  ## students in each state on each day
  daily <- as.data.table(t(apply(S, 1, function(r) tabulate(factor(r, ALL_STATES), length(ALL_STATES)))))
  setnames(daily, ALL_STATES); daily[, day := .I]

  list(edges = e[, run := seed], students = st[, run := seed], runs = runs, daily = daily,
       tr = tr, grades = gr, S = S)
}
detail_scenario <- function(school, vacc, strategy) {
  keys <- c("edges", "students", "runs", "daily")
  f <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("crn_detail3_%s_%s_%s_n%d_%s.csv", school, vacc * 100,
                                      gsub("/", "-", strategy), N_DETAIL, keys))
  if (all(file.exists(f))) return(setNames(lapply(f, fread), keys))
  m <- build_model(school, vacc, parse_strat(strategy), record = TRUE)
  out <- lapply(seq_len(N_DETAIL), function(sd) detail_run(m, sd)[keys])
  res <- lapply(keys[1:3], function(k) rbindlist(lapply(out, `[[`, k)))
  daily <- rbindlist(lapply(out, `[[`, "daily"))[, lapply(.SD, mean), by = day]
  res <- c(res, list(daily)); names(res) <- keys
  for (k in seq_along(keys)) fwrite(res[[k]], f[k])
  res
}
```

```{r detail-simulate}
DET <- list()
for (s in SCHOOLS) for (st in DETAIL_STRATS) {
  r <- detail_scenario(s, FIG_VACC, st)
  for (k in names(r)) r[[k]][, `:=`(school = s, strategy = st)]
  DET[[paste(s, st)]] <- r
}
DE <- rbindlist(lapply(DET, `[[`, "edges"))
DS <- rbindlist(lapply(DET, `[[`, "students"))
DR <- rbindlist(lapply(DET, `[[`, "runs"))
DD <- rbindlist(lapply(DET, `[[`, "daily"))
for (d in list(DE, DS, DR, DD))
  d[, `:=`(school = factor(school, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(strategy, DETAIL_STRATS))]
```

## Model behaviour in the simulations

How the rules above play out in `r N_DETAIL` outbreaks per school and
strategy (`r scales::percent(FIG_VACC)` vaccinated).

```{r behaviour-durations}
dur <- DS[, .(
  `Infected students`               = format(.N, big.mark = ","),
  `Latent days: mean (median)`      = sprintf("%.1f (%.0f)", mean(latent_days, na.rm = TRUE), median(latent_days, na.rm = TRUE)),
  `Latent more than 21 days`        = pct0(mean(latent_days > 21, na.rm = TRUE)),
  `Contagious days: mean (median)`  = sprintf("%.1f (%.0f)", mean(contag_days[contag_days > 0]), median(contag_days[contag_days > 0])),
  `Contagious days spent at school` = sprintf("%.1f", mean(contag_school[contag_days > 0])),
  `Rash noticed (isolated)`         = pct0(mean(isolated)),
  `Hospitalized`                    = pct0(mean(hosp))), by = .(Strategy = strategy)]
setorder(dur, Strategy)
knitr::kable(dur, align = "lrrrrrrr",
  caption = "Disease course of infected students (all schools pooled). Latent and contagious days are the same under every strategy (fair pairs); only the days spent at school change.")

stays <- DR[, .(`1 day`        = sprintf("%.1f", mean(stays_1)),
                `2-6 days`     = sprintf("%.1f", mean(stays_2_6)),
                `7-20 days`    = sprintf("%.1f", mean(stays_7_20)),
                `21+ days`     = sprintf("%.1f", mean(stays_21p)),
                `Healthy student-days at home` = sprintf("%.0f", mean(healthy_days_home))),
            by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy)]
setorder(stays, School, Strategy)
knitr::kable(stays, align = "llrrrrr",
  caption = "Stays at home in quarantine per outbreak, by length (all students). 0-day tiers produce 1-day stays; 2-6 days come from cases detected on consecutive days.")
```

## What is the same in a fair pair, and what is not

Two runs with the same seed under two strategies (say 21/21/21 and 21/0/0):

| | Same in both runs? |
|---|---|
| School, grades, number of students, contact matrix (how often grades mix), transmission rate | **Same** |
| Which students are vaccinated, and who the first case is | **Same** |
| Which vaccinated students are protected (the vaccine is all-or-nothing: each vaccinated student is either fully protected for the whole run, with probability equal to the vaccine efficacy, or not at all) | **Same** |
| Each student's disease course, counted from the day they are infected: days latent, days contagious, day the rash is noticed, hospitalization | **Same** |
| For every pair of students on every day: the coin "do they meet?" and the coin "does this meeting infect?" | **Same coins** |
| Who is at home on each day | **Different**: this is the strategy |
| The chance that two students at school meet | **Can differ**: each student's contacts per day with a grade are shared out among the students of that grade *who are at school*. When classmates are at home, the students left at school meet each other more often. The coin is the same, but the bar it must pass is not. |
| Who gets infected, and on which day | **Different** after the first detection, as a consequence of the rows above |

There is **no fixed friendship network**: the model does not decide in advance
which students are friends. Students mix at random by grade each day, at the
rates of the contact matrix. What fair pairs fix is the *dice*: if students X
and Y are both at school on day 38 and X is contagious, whether they meet and
whether Y is infected is decided by the same coins under both strategies.

Because who is at home differs, the two outbreaks start to differ after the
first detection. Later cases are detected on different days, which sends
different students home at different times, so the differences grow. The
section *Why does an infection happen under one strategy but not the other?*
below counts how often each reason occurs.

## Is the comparison really fair?

Students infected on the same day under two different strategies should have
the same latent and contagious days.

```{r fairness-check}
fairness <- local({
  sc <- if ("Middle" %in% SCHOOLS) "Middle" else SCHOOLS[1]
  mA <- build_model(sc, 0.6, c(21, 21, 21), TRUE)
  mB <- build_model(sc, 0.6, c(21, 0, 0), TRUE)
  course <- function(S, ids) vapply(ids, function(i) {
    d <- which(S[, i + 1L] %in% c("Prodromal", "Quarantined Prodromal"))
    if (length(d)) paste(min(d), length(d)) else NA_character_ }, character(1))
  res <- rbindlist(lapply(1:200, function(sd) {
    rec$days <- list(); run(mA, ndays = N_DAYS, seed = sd)
    SA <- do.call(rbind, rec$days); tA <- as.data.table(get_transmissions(mA))
    rec$days <- list(); run(mB, ndays = N_DAYS, seed = sd)
    SB <- do.call(rbind, rec$days); tB <- as.data.table(get_transmissions(mB))
    both <- merge(tA, tB, by = "target")[date.x == date.y]
    if (!nrow(both)) return(NULL)
    data.table(same = course(SA, both$target) == course(SB, both$target))
  }))
  res <- res[!is.na(same)]
  data.table(School = sc, `Seeds` = 200, `Students compared` = nrow(res),
             `Same latent and contagious days (21/21/21 vs 21/0/0)` = scales::percent(mean(res$same), 0.1))
})
knitr::kable(fairness)
```

This should be 100% (students still latent on the last day under both
strategies have no contagious period yet and are left out). With the normal
package it is only about 60%.

```{r design}
design <- rbind(
  data.table(set = "novac", strategy = unname(STRATS_NOVAC),
             label = names(STRATS_NOVAC), vacc = 0),
  CJ(set = "tiered", strategy = STRATS_TIERED, vacc = VACCS_TIERED,
     sorted = FALSE)[, label := strategy][]
)
design[, ref := REFERENCE[set]]
```

```{r simulate}
## Every scenario uses seeds 1..N_PAIRS, so seed k is the same outbreak start
## (same first case, same vaccinated students) under every strategy.
sim_scenario <- function(school, vacc, strategy) {
  f <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("crn_%s_%s_%s_n%d.csv", school, vacc * 100,
                                      gsub("/", "-", strategy), N_PAIRS))
  if (file.exists(f)) return(fread(f))
  m <- build_model(school, vacc, parse_strat(strategy))
  out <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(N_PAIRS), function(sd) {
    run(m, ndays = N_DAYS, seed = sd)
    h <- as.data.table(get_hist_total(m))
    data.table(seed = sd,
               size = nrow(get_transmissions(m)),                       # students infected
               healthy_days_home = h[state == "Quarantined Susceptible", sum(counts)])
  }))
  fwrite(out, f)
  out
}

sims <- rbindlist(lapply(SCHOOLS, function(s)
  rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(design)), function(i) {
    d <- design[i]
    cbind(school = s, d, sim_scenario(s, d$vacc, d$strategy))
  }))))
```

```{r tabulate}
## Pair every run with the reference run that has the same seed
ref_runs <- sims[strategy == ref, .(school, set, vacc, seed,
                                    size_ref = size, days_ref = healthy_days_home)]
paired <- ref_runs[sims, on = .(school, set, vacc, seed)]

## Wilson interval for one proportion
wilson_ci <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) {
  p <- x / n; den <- 1 + z^2 / n
  c0 <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / den
  hw <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / den
  list(lo = c0 - hw, hi = c0 + hw)
}

## Difference of two PAIRED proportions (same seeds), p_new - p_ref,
## Newcombe (1998) hybrid score interval for paired data (method 10).
newcombe_paired <- function(y_new, y_ref) {
  n <- length(y_new)
  a <- sum(y_new & y_ref);  b <- sum(y_new & !y_ref)
  c <- sum(!y_new & y_ref); d <- sum(!y_new & !y_ref)
  p1 <- (a + b) / n; p2 <- (a + c) / n
  w1 <- wilson_ci(a + b, n); w2 <- wilson_ci(a + c, n)
  den <- sqrt(as.numeric(a + b) * (c + d) * (a + c) * (b + d))
  phi <- if (den > 0) (a * d - b * c) / den else 0
  D <- p1 - p2
  dl <- (p1 - w1$lo)^2 - 2 * phi * (p1 - w1$lo) * (w2$hi - p2) + (w2$hi - p2)^2
  du <- (w1$hi - p1)^2 - 2 * phi * (w1$hi - p1) * (p2 - w2$lo) + (p2 - w2$lo)^2
  list(diff = D, lo = D - sqrt(max(dl, 0)), hi = D + sqrt(max(du, 0)))
}

fmt_pct  <- function(p) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * p)
fmt_diff <- function(d) { s <- function(v) sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * v)
                          sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", s(d$diff), s(d$lo), s(d$hi)) }
fmt_mean_diff <- function(x) {
  m <- mean(x); se <- sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
  sprintf("%+.2f (%+.2f to %+.2f)", m, m - 1.96 * se, m + 1.96 * se)
}

PROB_COLS <- paste0("P(e", THRESHOLDS, ")")
DIFF_COLS <- paste0("Difference P(e", THRESHOLDS, ")")

## Table A: outbreak probabilities and paired differences
tabA <- paired[, {
  out <- list(n = .N)
  for (i in seq_along(THRESHOLDS)) {
    k <- THRESHOLDS[i]
    out[[PROB_COLS[i]]] <- fmt_pct(mean(size >= k))
    out[[DIFF_COLS[i]]] <- if (strategy[1] == ref[1]) "Reference" else
      fmt_diff(newcombe_paired(size >= k, size_ref >= k))
  }
  out
}, by = .(school, set, vacc, strategy, label, ref)]

## Table B: run-by-run comparison with the reference (same seed)
tabB <- paired[, .(
  `Mean cases`               = sprintf("%.1f", mean(size)),
  `Mean difference in cases` = if (strategy[1] == ref[1]) "Reference" else fmt_mean_diff(size - size_ref),
  `Fewer cases than reference` = if (strategy[1] == ref[1]) "" else fmt_pct(mean(size < size_ref)),
  `Same cases`                 = if (strategy[1] == ref[1]) "" else fmt_pct(mean(size == size_ref)),
  `More cases than reference`  = if (strategy[1] == ref[1]) "" else fmt_pct(mean(size > size_ref)),
  `Healthy student-days at home` = sprintf("%.0f", mean(healthy_days_home))
), by = .(school, set, vacc, strategy, label, ref)]

unvacc <- function(s, v) as.integer(round(sum(ENROLLMENT[[s]]) * (1 - v)))
for (d in list(tabA, tabB)) {
  d[, `Unvaccinated students` := mapply(unvacc, school, vacc)]
  d[, ord := fifelse(set == "novac", match(strategy, STRATS_NOVAC), match(strategy, STRATS_TIERED))]
  setorder(d, school, set, vacc, ord)
}

showA <- function(d, first = "Strategy")
  knitr::kable(d[, c("label", "Unvaccinated students", PROB_COLS, DIFF_COLS), with = FALSE],
               col.names = c(first, "Unvaccinated students", PROB_COLS, DIFF_COLS),
               align = c("l", rep("r", 1 + 2 * length(THRESHOLDS))))
showB <- function(d, first = "Strategy", with_vacc = FALSE) {
  cols <- c(if (with_vacc) "Coverage", "label", "Mean cases", "Mean difference in cases",
            "Fewer cases than reference", "Same cases", "More cases than reference",
            "Healthy student-days at home")
  if (with_vacc) d <- copy(d)[, Coverage := vacc_lab(vacc)]
  knitr::kable(d[, cols, with = FALSE],
               col.names = c(if (with_vacc) "Coverage", first, cols[-(1:(1 + with_vacc))]),
               align = c(if (with_vacc) "l", "l", rep("r", 6)))
}

fwrite(tabA, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("crn_tableA_n%d.csv", N_PAIRS)))
fwrite(tabB, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("crn_tableB_n%d.csv", N_PAIRS)))
```

## How to read the tables

**Table A (outbreak probability).** P(eK) is the share of outbreaks with at
least K infected students. *Difference* is the strategy minus the reference
(*No quarantine* without vaccination, *21/21/21* in the tiered tables), in
**percentage points** with a 95% confidence interval for **paired** data
(Newcombe's hybrid score method; outbreaks are paired by seed). A positive
value means more outbreaks than the reference; if the interval includes 0 the
two cannot be told apart with this many outbreaks.

**Table B (run by run).** For each seed, the strategy's outbreak is compared
with the reference **on the same outbreak**:

- *Mean difference in cases*: average extra (+) or fewer () infected students than the reference, with a 95% interval.
- *Fewer / Same / More cases than reference*: how often this strategy did better, the same, or worse **on the same outbreak**. Because everything else is identical, a "More" outbreak is a real effect of the strategy, not chance.
- *Healthy student-days at home*: average days healthy students spent in quarantine per outbreak (the cost).

*Unvaccinated students* = enrolment × (1  coverage). Only these students are
quarantined.

## Results by school

```{r results, results='asis'}
for (s in SCHOOLS) {

  cat("**No vaccination: which single tier to quarantine** (compared with no quarantine)\n\n")
  print(showA(tabA[school == s & set == "novac"], "Scenario"))
  cat("\n\n")
  print(showB(tabB[school == s & set == "novac"], "Scenario"))

  cat("\n\n**Tiered strategies (high/medium/low days): outbreak probability**, compared with 21/21/21 at the same coverage\n\n")
  for (v in VACCS_TIERED) {
    cat(sprintf("\n\n*%s vaccinated*\n\n", vacc_lab(v)))
    print(showA(tabA[school == s & set == "tiered" & vacc == v]))
  }

  cat("\n\n**Tiered strategies: run by run against 21/21/21 on the same outbreak**\n\n")
  print(showB(tabB[school == s & set == "tiered"], with_vacc = TRUE))
}
```

## Inside the outbreaks: where do infections come from?

The tables above count cases. This part looks **inside** the outbreaks, using
who infected whom and every student's state on every day
(`r scales::percent(FIG_VACC)` vaccinated, `r N_DETAIL` fair pairs per school
and strategy). Every infection is put into one of four groups, according to
where the **infector** was before passing it on:

| Group | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Before anyone was detected** | happened before the first case was found. No strategy can act yet, so this is the same under every strategy. |
| **From a student never sent home** | after detection, by a student who was never in quarantine before infecting. On every detection day **all** unvaccinated students at school are sent home (the low-risk tier covers everyone else), so in practice these are **vaccinated students whose vaccine failed**: vaccinated students are never quarantined. |
| **From a student sent home only briefly** | the infector's longest stay at home was 1 to `r MIN_HOME - 1` days, typically the single day of a 0-day quarantine, or a few single days when cases were detected on consecutive days. In the model this **is** a quarantine, so it is shown separately rather than hidden. |
| **From a student back from a real quarantine** | the infector had been home `r MIN_HOME`+ days in a row and came back still infected (released while still latent, or contagious). |

```{r fig-sources}
#| fig-width: 10
```

### Why do the strategies differ?

Change in infections per outbreak compared with 21/21/21 **on the same
outbreaks**, split by where the infections came from. This shows **which
group** makes one strategy end with more or fewer cases than another.

```{r why-differ}
per_kind <- DE[, .(n = .N / N_DETAIL), by = .(school, strategy, kind)]
per_kind <- CJ(school = factor(SCHOOLS, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(DETAIL_STRATS, DETAIL_STRATS), kind = KINDS)[
  per_kind, on = .(school, strategy, kind), n := i.n][is.na(n), n := 0]
ref_k <- per_kind[strategy == "21/21/21", .(school, kind, n_ref = n)]
why <- ref_k[per_kind, on = .(school, kind)][strategy != "21/21/21"]
why_w <- dcast(why, school + strategy ~ kind, value.var = "n", fun.aggregate = function(x) x[1])
why_d <- dcast(why[, d := n - n_ref], school + strategy ~ kind, value.var = "d")
setcolorder(why_d, c("school", "strategy", KINDS))
why_d[, Total := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = KINDS]
for (k in c(KINDS, "Total")) set(why_d, j = k, value = sprintf("%+.2f", why_d[[k]]))
setnames(why_d, c("school", "strategy"), c("School", "Strategy"))
knitr::kable(why_d, align = "llrrrrr",
  caption = "Extra (+) or fewer () infections per outbreak than 21/21/21, by where they came from.")
```

**How to read it, and what each column means for the reason behind a difference:**

- **Before anyone was detected** should be **0** for every strategy: fair pairs are identical until the first detection. Any difference here would point to a problem.
- **From a student never sent home**: infections by vaccinated students whose vaccine failed. No strategy can reach them, because vaccinated students are never quarantined. Differences here are indirect: a strategy that lets the outbreak grow exposes more vaccinated students, so more of them are infected and pass it on.
- **From a student sent home only briefly**: the main effect of short medium/low-risk quarantine. A 0-day quarantine keeps a student home for **one day**, but a student is contagious for about four days on average and the latent period is long, so a one-day stay rarely covers the contagious days. These students come back and infect others. Longer medium/low-risk quarantine (7 or 14 days) moves these students into the "real quarantine" groups or keeps their contagious days at home.
- **From a student back from a real quarantine**: infections by students released after 7+ days while still infected. This can be **larger** under stricter strategies, because more infected students are quarantined and released together (and the model's latent period has a long tail, so some are still latent after 21 days; see document 6). It shows the cost side of quarantining more students.
- **Total** equals the difference in mean cases in Table B.

### What happened to each infected student?

```{r table-students}
t2 <- DS[, c(lapply(GROUPS2, function(g) pct0(mean(group == g))),
             lapply(GROUPS2[2:4], function(g) { x <- n_infected[group == g]
                                                if (length(x)) sprintf("%.1f", mean(x)) else "-" })),
         by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy)]
setnames(t2, 3:10, c(GROUPS2, paste("Others infected by each:", tolower(GROUPS2[2:4]))))
setorder(t2, School, Strategy)
knitr::kable(t2, align = "llrrrrrrrr",
  caption = "Table 2. What happened to each infected student (first case excluded), and how many others they infected on average.")
```

- *Contagious period fully at home*: the student was at home (quarantine) for all their contagious days, so quarantine fully worked for them.
- *Back from a real quarantine still infected*: home `r MIN_HOME`+ days in a row while infected, but contagious at school after returning.
- *Home only 1-`r MIN_HOME - 1` days while infected, contagious at school*: at home only briefly while infected, and contagious at school for at least one day. This is mainly the 1-day stays of a 0-day quarantine, plus students who were sent home partway through their contagious period (they had already been contagious at school; this is why the group is not empty under 21/21/21).
- *Never sent home while infected*: at school for the whole infection.
- *Still latent on the last day*: infected near the end of the simulation, not yet contagious.

### Why does an infection happen under one strategy but not the other?

Take every infection "student X infects student Y on day d" where Y is
infected on day d under one strategy but **not** under the other, on the same
outbreak. Since the dice
are the same, there must be a concrete reason. Looking at the other strategy on
the start of day d, the reasons are checked in this order:

1. **X was infected on a different day there (or not at all).** X's own infection already differed, so X is contagious on different days (or never).
2. **X was at home that day** (in quarantine while contagious).
3. **Y was already infected** there (by someone else, earlier).
4. **Y was at home that day** (in quarantine).
5. **Both at school, but a different chance of meeting.** X was contagious and Y was healthy at school under both strategies, but a different number of X's classmates were at school, so the chance that they meet was different (see the table at the top).
6. **Other**: none of the above. This should be **0%**: if X was contagious and Y healthy, both at school with the same chance of meeting, the same dice give the same result. It is a check that the comparison is fair.

```{r why-pair}
N_WHY <- min(N_DETAIL, as.integer(Sys.getenv("N_WHY", unset = 300)))
AT_SCHOOL <- c("Susceptible", "Latent", "Prodromal", "Recovered")
WHY <- c("X infected on a different day (or not at all)", "X at home that day",
         "Y already infected", "Y at home that day",
         "Both at school, different chance of meeting", "Other")

## infections under run A that do not happen under run B, with the reason
why_one_way <- function(A, B) {
  eA <- A$tr[source >= 0]; eB <- B$tr[source >= 0]
  e <- eA[!eB, on = .(target, date)]        # Y infected on day d under A but not under B
  if (!nrow(e)) return(data.table(reason = character(0)))
  infday <- function(r, i) { d <- r$tr[target == i, date]; if (length(d)) d[1] else NA_integer_ }
  rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(e)), function(k) {
    x <- e$source[k]; y <- e$target[k]; d <- e$date[k]; r0 <- max(d - 1L, 1L)   # state at the start of day d
    g <- A$grades[x + 1L]
    nA <- sum(A$grades == g & A$S[r0, ] %in% AT_SCHOOL); nB <- sum(B$grades == g & B$S[r0, ] %in% AT_SCHOOL)
    xB <- B$S[r0, x + 1L]; yB <- B$S[r0, y + 1L]
    data.table(reason = fcase(
      !identical(infday(A, x), infday(B, x)),  WHY[1],
      xB == "Quarantined Prodromal",            WHY[2],
      !(yB %in% c("Susceptible", "Quarantined Susceptible")), WHY[3],
      yB == "Quarantined Susceptible",          WHY[4],
      nA != nB,                                 WHY[5],
      default =                                 WHY[6]))
  }))
}
why_scenario <- function(school, vacc, strat_b) {
  f <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, sprintf("crn_why_%s_%s_%s_n%d.csv", school, vacc * 100,
                                      gsub("/", "-", strat_b), N_WHY))
  if (file.exists(f)) return(fread(f))
  mA <- build_model(school, vacc, parse_strat("21/21/21"), record = TRUE)
  mB <- build_model(school, vacc, parse_strat(strat_b),   record = TRUE)
  out <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(N_WHY), function(sd) {
    A <- detail_run(mA, sd); B <- detail_run(mB, sd)
    rbind(why_one_way(A, B)[, direction := "only_A"],
          why_one_way(B, A)[, direction := "only_B"])
  }))
  fwrite(out, f)
  out
}
WY <- rbindlist(lapply(SCHOOLS, function(s) rbindlist(lapply(setdiff(DETAIL_STRATS, "21/21/21"), function(st)
  why_scenario(s, FIG_VACC, st)[, `:=`(school = s, strategy = st)]))))
WY[, `:=`(school = factor(school, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(strategy, DETAIL_STRATS),
          reason = factor(reason, WHY))]

why_tab <- function(dir) {
  d <- WY[direction == dir, .N, by = .(school, strategy, reason)]
  d <- CJ(school = factor(SCHOOLS, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(setdiff(DETAIL_STRATS, "21/21/21"), DETAIL_STRATS),
          reason = factor(WHY, WHY))[d, on = .(school, strategy, reason), N := i.N][is.na(N), N := 0L]
  w <- d[, .(`Per outbreak` = sprintf("%.2f", sum(N) / N_WHY),
             reason = reason, share = if (sum(N)) pct0(N / sum(N)) else "-"), by = .(school, strategy)]
  w <- dcast(w, school + strategy + `Per outbreak` ~ reason, value.var = "share")
  setnames(w, c("school", "strategy"), c("School", "Other strategy"))
  setorder(w, School, `Other strategy`)
  w
}
knitr::kable(why_tab("only_A"), align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 7)),
  caption = sprintf("Infections that happen under 21/21/21 but NOT under the other strategy (same outbreak): how many per outbreak, and why they did not happen under the other strategy (%d fair pairs).", N_WHY))
knitr::kable(why_tab("only_B"), align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 7)),
  caption = "Infections that happen under the other strategy but NOT under 21/21/21: how many per outbreak, and why they did not happen under 21/21/21.")
```

**How to read these two tables.** *Per outbreak* is how many infections, on
average, happen under one strategy only. Comparing the two tables gives the
net effect: for 21/0/0, many more infections happen only under 21/0/0 than only
under 21/21/21. The reason columns explain each one. Most differences are
chains: once one infection differs (reason 1), everything that follows it
differs too. Reasons 2 and 4 are the direct effect of quarantine: someone was
at home on that day under one strategy and not the other. Reason 5 is a side
effect of the model's contact rule: when many students are at home, those left
at school meet each other more often; it is rare.

**So why does stricter quarantine sometimes give more infections?** Not
because of chance: the dice are the same. It is because quarantine changes
*when* students are at home, and the outbreaks then follow different paths:

- a student sent home for 21 days while still latent can come back and become contagious at school later (the long latent tail of the model), on days when under the shorter strategy they were at home for a different reason, or not infected at all;
- once one infection differs, the cases that follow it, the days they are detected, and therefore who is sent home and when, all differ (reason 1).

## Grade-to-grade spread (`r FIG_A` vs `r FIG_B`)

Each circle is a grade; arrow width = average number of infections per
outbreak from one grade into another. The number inside each circle is the
average number of infections inside that grade.

```{r fig-grade-flow}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
FL <- DE[strategy %in% c(FIG_A, FIG_B)]
flow <- FL[, .(per_run = .N / N_DETAIL), by = .(school, strategy, src_grade, tgt_grade)]
flow[, `:=`(school = as.character(school), strategy = as.character(strategy))]
pos_grade <- function(n) { a <- pi / 2 - 2 * pi * (seq_len(n) - 1) / n
                           data.table(grade = seq_len(n), x = cos(a), y = sin(a)) }
nodes <- rbindlist(lapply(SCHOOLS, function(s) cbind(school = s, pos_grade(length(ENROLLMENT[[s]])))))
nodes <- CJ(school = SCHOOLS, strategy = c(FIG_A, FIG_B))[nodes, on = "school", allow.cartesian = TRUE]
inside <- flow[src_grade == tgt_grade, .(school, strategy, grade = src_grade, inside = per_run)]
nodes <- inside[nodes, on = .(school, strategy, grade)][is.na(inside), inside := 0]
arr <- flow[src_grade != tgt_grade]
arr[nodes, on = .(school, strategy, src_grade = grade), `:=`(x0 = i.x, y0 = i.y)]
arr[nodes, on = .(school, strategy, tgt_grade = grade), `:=`(x1 = i.x, y1 = i.y)]
shrink <- function(a, b, f = 0.2) a + (b - a) * f
arr[, `:=`(xs = shrink(x0, x1), ys = shrink(y0, y1), xe = shrink(x1, x0), ye = shrink(y1, y0))]
cross_tot <- arr[, .(cross = sum(per_run)), by = .(school, strategy)]
for (d in list(nodes, arr, cross_tot)) d[, `:=`(school = factor(school, SCHOOLS), strategy = factor(strategy, c(FIG_A, FIG_B)))]

p_flow <- ggplot() +
  geom_curve(data = arr, aes(xs, ys, xend = xe, yend = ye, linewidth = per_run),
             colour = "#D85A30", alpha = 0.7, curvature = 0.15,
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed")) +
  geom_point(data = nodes, aes(x, y), size = 13, shape = 21, fill = "#F1EFE8", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_text(data = nodes, aes(x, y, label = sprintf("G%d\n%.1f", grade, inside)), size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = cross_tot, aes(0, -1.45, label = sprintf("%.2f jumps per outbreak", cross)), size = 3.3) +
  facet_grid(strategy ~ school) +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.2, 3), name = "Infections per outbreak\ninto another grade") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-1.4, 1.4), ylim = c(-1.6, 1.3)) +
  labs(title = "Infections inside and between grades (average per outbreak)") +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, "07_grade_flow.png"), p_flow, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
p_flow

t3 <- DE[src_grade != tgt_grade, c(list(`Jumps per outbreak` = sprintf("%.2f", .N / N_DETAIL)),
                                   setNames(lapply(KINDS, function(k) pct0(mean(kind == k))), KINDS)),
         by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy)]
t3 <- DR[size > 1, .(`Outbreaks that stayed in one grade` = pct0(mean(grades_reached == 1))),
         by = .(School = school, Strategy = strategy)][t3, on = .(School, Strategy)]
setorder(t3, School, Strategy)
knitr::kable(t3, align = "llrrrrrr",
  caption = "Table 3. Infections that jump into another grade, and where the infector had been (all strategies).")
```

## One fair example per school

For each school, one outbreak where `r FIG_A` ended with **more** cases than
`r FIG_B`, and one where it ended with **fewer** (the largest such difference
among outbreaks with at most 60 cases). Everything is identical in the two
runs except who is at home, so every difference is caused by the strategy.
Each dot is an infected student (left to right = day infected, rows = grade);
filled dots were infected under both strategies, open dots under this
strategy only. Arrows are coloured by where the infector had been.

The first two figures show only **who infected whom, and on which day**. The
third figure adds **what state every infected student is in on every day, and
when they are at home**:

- one row per student infected under either strategy; the same student is on the same row in both panels;
- the coloured bar is the disease state: grey = latent, red = contagious (the only state that infects), light purple = rash at school, purple = isolated or in hospital; no bar = healthy or recovered;
- the tan background marks days at home in quarantine, including days at home while still healthy;
- a dotted row means this student was never infected under that strategy;
- arrows run from the infector's row to the new case's row on the day of infection, coloured as above. An arrow always starts from a red (contagious) bar on a day without tan background, because only contagious students at school infect.

```{r example-setup}
draw_pair <- function(school, seed, tag) {
  mA <- build_model(school, FIG_VACC, parse_strat(FIG_A), record = TRUE)
  mB <- build_model(school, FIG_VACC, parse_strat(FIG_B), record = TRUE)
  rA <- detail_run(mA, seed); rB <- detail_run(mB, seed)
  both <- intersect(rA$tr$target, rB$tr$target)
  ng <- length(ENROLLMENT[[school]])
  panel <- function(r, lab) {
    p <- r$tr[, .(id = target, x = date, grade = r$grades[target + 1L])]
    setorder(p, x, id); p[, k := seq_len(.N) - 1L, by = grade]
    p[, y := grade + ((k %% 5) - 2) * 0.13][, in_both := id %in% both]
    e <- copy(r$edges)
    e[p, on = .(source = id), `:=`(x0 = i.x, y0 = i.y)]
    e[p, on = .(target = id), `:=`(x1 = i.x, y1 = i.y)]
    n <- table(factor(e$kind, KINDS))
    ttl <- sprintf("%s: %d infected  (%d before detection, %d from never sent home, %d from briefly home, %d from back after a real quarantine)",
                   lab, nrow(r$tr), n[1], n[2], n[3], n[4])
    list(p = p[, panel := ttl], e = e[, panel := ttl])
  }
  a <- panel(rA, FIG_A); b <- panel(rB, FIG_B)
  P <- rbind(a$p, b$p); E <- rbind(a$e, b$e); lv <- c(a$p$panel[1], b$p$panel[1])
  P[, panel := factor(panel, lv)]; E[, `:=`(panel = factor(panel, lv), kind = factor(kind, KINDS))]
  g <- ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = seq(1.5, ng - 0.5), colour = "grey92") +
    geom_segment(data = E, aes(x0, y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, colour = kind), linewidth = 0.6,
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.6, "mm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_point(data = P, aes(x, y, shape = in_both), colour = "grey25", fill = "white", size = 1.8, stroke = 0.9) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21), name = NULL,
                       labels = c(`TRUE` = "Infected under both strategies", `FALSE` = "Infected under this strategy only")) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = KIND_COLS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_len(ng), labels = paste("Grade", seq_len(ng)),
                       limits = c(0.5, ng + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, N_DAYS)) +
    labs(x = "Day infected", y = NULL,
         title = sprintf("%s school, %s vaccinated, seed %d", school, scales::percent(FIG_VACC), seed)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", panel.grid = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0), plot.title.position = "plot")
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("07_example_%s_%s_seed%d.png", school, tag, seed)),
         g, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 150, bg = "white")

  ## grades as clusters, both strategies side by side
  clusters <- function(r, lab) {
    gr <- r$grades; nd <- r$tr[, .(id = target, day = date, grade = gr[target + 1L])]
    nc <- if (ng <= 4) 2 else 3
    cen <- data.table(grade = seq_len(ng), cx = ((seq_len(ng) - 1) %% nc) * 2.3,
                      cy = -((seq_len(ng) - 1) %/% nc) * 2.3)
    setorder(nd, day, id); nd[, k := seq_len(.N), by = grade]
    nd[, n := .N, by = grade]
    nd[, `:=`(rr = 0.8 * sqrt((k - 0.5) / n), th = k * 2.39996)]          # sunflower layout
    nd[cen, on = "grade", `:=`(x = i.cx + rr * cos(th), y = i.cy + rr * sin(th))]
    e <- copy(r$edges)
    e[nd, on = .(source = id), `:=`(x0 = i.x, y0 = i.y)]
    e[nd, on = .(target = id), `:=`(x1 = i.x, y1 = i.y)]
    circ <- cen[, .(x = cx + cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 80)),
                    y = cy + sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 80))), by = grade]
    lab_dt <- cen[, .(x = cx, y = cy + 1.15, label = sprintf("Grade %d: %d", grade,
                      vapply(grade, function(g) sum(nd$grade == g), integer(1))))]
    list(nd = nd[, panel := lab], e = e[, panel := lab], circ = circ[, panel := lab], lab = lab_dt[, panel := lab])
  }
  ca <- clusters(rA, FIG_A); cb <- clusters(rB, FIG_B)
  cmb <- function(k) { d <- rbind(ca[[k]], cb[[k]]); d[, panel := factor(panel, c(FIG_A, FIG_B))]; d }
  ND <- cmb("nd"); CE <- cmb("e"); CI <- cmb("circ"); LB <- cmb("lab")
  CE[, `:=`(jump = src_grade != tgt_grade, kind = factor(kind, KINDS))]
  g3 <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = CI, aes(x, y, group = grade), fill = "#F1EFE8") +
    geom_text(data = LB, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.2) +
    geom_segment(data = CE[jump == FALSE], aes(x0, y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), colour = "#D3D1C7", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_curve(data = CE[jump == TRUE], aes(x0, y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, colour = kind), linewidth = 1,
               curvature = 0.15, arrow = arrow(length = unit(2.2, "mm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_point(data = ND, aes(x, y), colour = "grey25", size = 1.3) +
    facet_wrap(~panel) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = KIND_COLS, name = "Jump into another grade:", drop = FALSE) +
    coord_equal() + theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Jumps between grades (%s school, seed %d). Grey lines = spread inside a grade.", school, seed)) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical", strip.text = element_text(size = 11))
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("07_grades_%s_%s_seed%d.png", school, tag, seed)),
         g3, width = 11, height = 6.5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
  g4 <- draw_states(school, seed, rA, rB)
  f4 <- file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("07_states_%s_%s_seed%d.png", school, tag, seed))
  ggsave(f4, g4, width = 14, height = attr(g4, "h"), dpi = 150, bg = "white", limitsize = FALSE)
  list(g, g3, f4)            # the tall day-by-day figure is shown from its file, at its own size
}

## ---- Day-by-day states of every infected student, both strategies ----------
STATE_GRP <- c(Latent = "Latent", `Quarantined Latent` = "Latent",
               Prodromal = "Contagious", `Quarantined Prodromal` = "Contagious",
               Rash = "Rash (at school, not contagious)",
               Isolated = "Isolated / hospital", `Isolated Recovered` = "Isolated / hospital",
               Hospitalized = "Isolated / hospital")
STATE_COLS <- c(Latent = "#9C9A92", Contagious = "#D85A30",
                `Rash (at school, not contagious)` = "#C9A0DC", `Isolated / hospital` = "#7F77DD")
draw_states <- function(school, seed, rA, rB) {
  runs <- list(rA, rB); names(runs) <- c(FIG_A, FIG_B)
  gr <- rA$grades
  ## students infected under either strategy (the first case included)
  inf <- rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(st) runs[[st]]$tr[, .(id = target, day = date, strategy = st)]))
  ids <- inf[, .(first = min(day)), by = id]
  ids[, grade := gr[id + 1L]]
  setorder(ids, grade, first, id)
  ids[, row := .I]
  ## one segment per run of the same state, per student and strategy
  seg <- rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(st) {
    S <- runs[[st]]$S
    rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ids)), function(k) {
      x <- S[, ids$id[k] + 1L]
      home <- x %in% QSTATES
      grp  <- unname(STATE_GRP[x]); grp[is.na(grp)] <- "none"
      r1 <- rle(grp); e1 <- cumsum(r1$lengths)
      r2 <- rle(home); e2 <- cumsum(r2$lengths)
      rbind(data.table(kind = "state", value = r1$values, from = e1 - r1$lengths + 1, to = e1),
            data.table(kind = "home", value = as.character(r2$values), from = e2 - r2$lengths + 1, to = e2)
      )[, `:=`(row = ids$row[k], strategy = st)]
    }))
  }))
  seg[, strategy := factor(strategy, c(FIG_A, FIG_B))]
  st_seg   <- seg[kind == "state" & value != "none"]
  home_seg <- seg[kind == "home" & value == "TRUE"]
  ## arrows: infector row -> target row, on the infection day
  ed <- rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(st) {
    e <- copy(runs[[st]]$edges)[, strategy := st]
    e[ids, on = .(source = id), r0 := i.row][ids, on = .(target = id), r1 := i.row]
  }))
  ed[, `:=`(strategy = factor(strategy, c(FIG_A, FIG_B)), kind = factor(kind, KINDS))]
  ## students never infected under a strategy: a thin dotted guide line
  notinf <- rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(st)
    ids[!id %in% runs[[st]]$tr$target, .(row, strategy = st)]))
  notinf[, strategy := factor(strategy, c(FIG_A, FIG_B))]
  gbreaks <- ids[, .(y = mean(row), lab = paste("Grade", grade[1])), by = grade]
  glines  <- ids[, .(y = max(row) + 0.5), by = grade][-.N]
  lab <- function(st) sprintf("%s: %d infected", st, nrow(runs[[st]]$tr))
  g <- ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = home_seg, aes(xmin = from - 0.5, xmax = to + 0.5, ymin = row - 0.45, ymax = row + 0.45),
              fill = "#F2D9A6", colour = NA) +
    geom_segment(data = notinf, aes(x = 0, xend = N_DAYS, y = row, yend = row),
                 colour = "grey85", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_rect(data = st_seg, aes(xmin = from - 0.5, xmax = to + 0.5, ymin = row - 0.28, ymax = row + 0.28,
                                 fill = value), colour = NA) +
    geom_hline(data = glines, aes(yintercept = y), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_curve(data = ed, aes(x = date, xend = date, y = r0, yend = r1, colour = kind),
               curvature = 0.25, linewidth = 0.45, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.3, "mm"), type = "closed")) +
    facet_wrap(~strategy, ncol = 2, labeller = as_labeller(setNames(sapply(c(FIG_A, FIG_B), lab), c(FIG_A, FIG_B)))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = STATE_COLS, name = "State", breaks = names(STATE_COLS)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = KIND_COLS, name = "Infection, by where the infector had been", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = gbreaks$y, labels = gbreaks$lab, expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.5, N_DAYS + 0.5), breaks = seq(0, N_DAYS, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 2), colour = guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 2)) +
    labs(x = "Day", y = NULL,
         title = sprintf("Day by day: %s school, %s vaccinated, seed %d", school, scales::percent(FIG_VACC), seed),
         subtitle = paste("One row per student infected under either strategy (same row in both panels).",
                          "Coloured bar = disease state; tan background = at home in quarantine (also while healthy);",
                          "dotted row = never infected under this strategy.", sep = "\n")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot",
          strip.text = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0))
  attr(g, "h") <- min(40, 3 + 0.16 * nrow(ids))
  g
}

## pick the seeds from the fair pairs already simulated above
pairs_fig <- merge(sims[vacc == FIG_VACC & strategy == FIG_A, .(school, seed, cases_A = size)],
                   sims[vacc == FIG_VACC & strategy == FIG_B, .(school, seed, cases_B = size)],
                   by = c("school", "seed"))
pick <- function(d) if (nrow(d)) d$seed[1] else NA_integer_
```

```{r examples, results='asis'}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
for (s in SCHOOLS) {
  d <- pairs_fig[school == s]
  ex <- list(
    list(tag = "A-worse", txt = sprintf("%s ended with MORE cases than %s", FIG_A, FIG_B),
         seed = pick(d[cases_A > cases_B & cases_A <= 60][order(-(cases_A - cases_B))]),
         share = mean(d$cases_A > d$cases_B)),
    list(tag = "A-better", txt = sprintf("%s ended with FEWER cases than %s", FIG_A, FIG_B),
         seed = pick(d[cases_A < cases_B & cases_B <= 60][order(-(cases_B - cases_A))]),
         share = mean(d$cases_A < d$cases_B)))
  cat(sprintf("\n\n### %s\n\n", s))
  for (x in ex) {
    if (is.na(x$seed)) { cat(sprintf("\n\nNo outbreak where %s.\n\n", x$txt)); next }
    cat(sprintf("\n\n**Example: %s** (this happened in %s of the %d fair pairs)\n\n",
                x$txt, pct0(x$share), nrow(d)))
    gg <- draw_pair(s, x$seed, x$tag)
    print(gg[[1]]); cat("\n\n"); print(gg[[2]]); cat("\n\n")
    cat("\n\n*Day by day: which state each infected student is in, and when they are at home.*\n\n")
    cat(sprintf("![](%s){width=100%%}\n\n", gg[[3]]))
  }
}
```

## Notes

- Outbreak size = number of students infected by day `r N_DAYS`, including the
  first case (one row per infection in the transmission record).
- The model's disease rules are unchanged; only the way random numbers are
  used is changed (common random numbers). Averages agree with the normal
  package within simulation error, but individual runs differ from it.
- Intervals reflect simulation (Monte Carlo) uncertainty only, not
  uncertainty in the model's assumptions (see document 6 for how the model's
  disease timing compares with real measles).
